text:
Maya Patel: quick heads-up — trying to repro the 2x token latency regression on batch=1 (RTX A5000). I captured an nsys trace but a bunch of CUDA kernels show as unknown (no symbols). anyone have a checklist for packaging symbols + torch.profiler output together?

Raj Verma: for nsys you usually need the stripped binary + the .sym file or unstripped build. if you don't have that we can still share a sanitized timeline but kernel names will be generic. did you build from the release wheel or a local dev build?

Maya Patel: release wheel (2026-03-05). build logs attached to the run. wondering if we should ask infra for the unstripped wheel from the CI artifact store.

Kevin Liu: if it's the release wheel we likely don't have full symbols on host. quick option: grab the container image ID and run `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/trace` against a small smoke run, then upload the .qdrep + `python -m torch.profiler` output. that helps match hotspots.

Maya Patel: noted. I'll re-run a tiny smoke and attach the qdrep. also want to include a flamegraph from py-spy for CPU threads — is that useful here?

Dan Cho: flamegraph helps for Python-side overheads (tokenization, pre/post processing). but the big regression looked GPU-side in the initial runs. please include both.

Sophie Ramos: tagging infra — @perf-bot can you grant maya read access to the CI artifacts bucket path `s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/wheels/2026-03-05/`? we need the unstripped wheel or debuginfo. :eyes:

perf-bot: Granted read access to maya.patel@redwood.com for s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/wheels/2026-03-05/ — expires in 24h. :white_check_mark:

Maya Patel: thanks! re-run in progress. putting checklist here so we don't miss anything: 1) small nsys capture (.qdrep + .sqlite) 2) unstripped wheel or build-id mapping 3) torch.profiler trace + chrome trace json 4) py-spy flamegraph for CPU 5) a short repro snippet + env (CUDA, driver, container SHA) — will upload to `gs://redwood-perf/threads/2165012345/` when done.

Kevin Liu: perfect. when you upload, add `--sensitive-scrub=true` tag if data contains customer prompts. we'll scrub env vars in the storage helper.

Maya Patel: uploaded artifacts: /gs/redwood-perf/threads/2165012345/{trace.qdrep,torchprof.json,pyspy.svg,env.txt}. sharing link now.

Raj Verma: grabbing the qdrep to run a quick nv-nsight parse. if I see unknown kernels I'll try matching build-ids against the unstripped wheel once you confirm access.

Dan Cho: if anyone wants to look at a minimized repro (5 tokens, batch=1) it's in the same folder as `repro.py`. also added the exact container SHA and driver versions in env.txt.

Sophie Ramos: FYI adding this to the perf board under "regression triage" and assigning to maya + kevin.

Maya Patel: sweet — ping me if you need anything else. thanks all. :pray:
